Priya: quick update from the nano-embed bring-up / quant experiment. ran fp16 vs int8 vs int4 (per-tensor and per-channel asymmetric) across wiki-short and our customer longtail.

Ken: nice, top-line numbers?

Priya: fp16 baseline recall@1 (wiki-short)=0.825, recall@10=0.947. int8 per-tensor: recall@1=0.803, int10=0.942. int4 per-tensor was brutal: r@1=0.712.

Jules: ouch int4. did you try per-channel scales?

Priya: yes--- per-channel asymmetric int4 improved to r@1=0.782 (r@10=0.931) after clipping outliers with 99.9pct percentile. so quant profile matters a lot.

Tom: what about indexing effects? HNSW params, efConstruction, efSearch?

Priya: default HNSW (M=16, efC=200, efS=64) kept. interestingly idflip analysis shows many failures are knn ordering flips rather than embedding collapse. increasing efSearch to 200 recovers ~0.012 r@1 for int4 PCQ.

Ken: so part of loss is search approximation + quant combined. can you isolate by running exact brute-force on quantized vectors?

Priya: ran brute-force cosine on quantized vectors: int4 PC asymmetric brute-force r@1=0.768 (vs 0.782 with hnsw tuned). suggests both quant noise + search approx.

Jules: did you attempt post-quant L2 renorm/temperature scaling?

Priya: yes. pipeline: quantize -> dequant -> L2 renorm. that recovered ~0.015 r@1 for int4-pc on wiki-short. on longtail set the gain was smaller (0.008) but stable.

Tom: any centroid drift / cluster metrics? silhouette etc?

Priya: silhouette fp16=0.59, int4_pc=0.53 after renorm. centroid cosine shift mean=-0.021, but tail classes show -0.035.

Ken: language / length strat?

Priya: long queries (>80 tok) worse: r@1 delta ~0.07 for int4; short queries (<12) near identical. low-frequency anchors and very domain-specific tokens get quantized poorly (high dynamic range).

Jules: action items?

Priya: 1) run per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric sweep (int4, int6, int8) 2) add pctile clipping pre-quant 3) try whitening (PCA 64) + renorm before indexing 4) isolate brute-force vs indexed losses per-profile 5) produce small repro set of idflips.

Tom: if per-channel asymmetric + renorm gets to within ~2% of fp16 on recall@1 we can add int4 as a "best-effort" onboarding profile but document tail sensitivity.

Ken: also add recommended HNSW efSearch tuning and a note about brute-force validation for onboarding.

Priya: will run sweep and upload uMAP snapshots + a tiny idflip repro (20 examples) to the model board. ETA 1.5h. ping me if you want the raw vectors.

Jules: thanks priya 1: good to have concrete mitigation steps for customers.

Priya: cheers :thumbsup:
